subject: NovaMed go-live: quota exception request + traffic model
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: NovaMed go-live: quota exception request + traffic model

Team —

Quick summary: NovaMed (pilot → GA) has confirmed a phased US launch on 2027-02-20. They expect a weekend ramp on day 1, with peak sustained traffic during business hours estimated in the attached model. Key asks from sales/CS: a temporary quota uplift and routing guardrails to keep latency <300ms P95 for critical flows.

Highlights from their forecast (see attached traffic_model.xlsx):
- Peak daily token volume (peak day): ~12–18M tokens/day (concentrated in a 6–8 hour window)
- Estimated average concurrency: 45–60 concurrent sessions for the core endpoint, bursty spikes up to ~220 concurrent for short windows
- Token distribution: 70% short prompts (~20–60 tokens), 30% long prompts (300–1200 tokens)

What we need from infra/product:
1) Temporary quota bump (per-route token throughput) and concurrent request caps to accommodate the above peak; propose a 4x baseline uplift for the first 72 hours with automatic ramp-down/rollback.
2) A canary plan + throttling policy (preferred split-by-route so we can route non-critical requests to a lower-tier model).
3) Warm-up playbook: recommended warm-up traffic pattern and timing to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

Deadline: customer expects confirmation to proceed with deployment by EOD Friday (2027-02-12). Can we have a recommended quota number and any blockers by tomorrow 2pm PT?

Attachments: [Attachment: traffic_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovaMed go-live: quota exception request + traffic model

Lauren — thanks for the model and the clear ask. A few clarifying Qs from runtime:

1) Concurrency vs RPS — when you say "220 concurrent", is that long-lived websocket/chat sessions or short HTTP requests? The impact on KV cache and memory is different.
2) Model pinning — do they require a single pinned model (e.g., redwood-v2-large) or are they ok with a lower-cost fall-back for non-critical traffic?
3) SLA tolerance — is the <300ms P95 a hard requirement for every request, or only on the subset labeled as "critical" in the spreadsheet?

Preliminary capacity notes:
- For 220 concurrent long-lived sessions with the long-prompt distribution listed, we should request a 3.5–5x temporary throughput uplift on the dedicated pool serving them. That covers headroom for queued bursts and autoscaler latency.
- Autoscaling warm-up: recommend a 24-hour progressive warm-up starting at 30% baseline, incrementing every 3 hours with synthetic replay of the "long prompt" distribution to populate KV cache.
- We can implement route-based fallback to a quantized variant (redwood-v2-large-8bit) for non-critical flows; that preserves latency but reduces cost.

Blockers: we need confirmation on concurrency semantics and final model selection. Once confirmed I can open the quota exception ticket with SRE and draft the warm-up job.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovaMed go-live: quota exception request + traffic model

Adding product/readiness perspective —

Thanks Lauren + Rishi. Product notes and recommended rollout:
- Canary window: 6 hours on the GA launch day with a 10% fraction of traffic routed to the new pipeline. During canary, we will run synthetic checks for correctness and token accounting.
- Routing policy: create an explicit route for "nova_critical" (P95 <300ms target) and "nova_best_effort" for other flows. We should enable automatic fallback rules to the quantized model after latency >350ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Quota numbers: given Rishi's guidance and the token mix, product is comfortable with the proposed 4x uplift for 72 hours, but we want a hard upper cap on spend/sustained throughput (please include thresholds).
- Telemetry: ensure tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown are enabled for both routes and we add NovaMed evals to Redwood Optimize to watch quality drift during the warm-up.

I'll create the console rollout plan and post the drive link here: https://drive.redwood/novamed/launch-runbook (will add canary config).

Marissa Cole
Staff Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Claire Young <claire.young@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 15:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovaMed go-live: quota exception request + traffic model

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and confirmations so we can respond to NovaMed:

1) Quota exception: request 4x per-route token throughput for the primary "nova_critical" route for the first 72 hours (auto-roll back to baseline after 72h). Rishi to raise the SRE ticket with the numbers below.
2) Concurrency: treat the 220 number as "burst concurrency" (short spikes). We'll configure autoscaler headroom per Rishi's guidance and run the 24-hour warm-up starting 2027-02-18 09:00 PT.
3) Model routing: canary config as Marissa outlined — 6-hour canary with 10% traffic, fallback to quantized variant if latency breach occurs.
4) Spend cap: set soft threshold at $X/day and hard cap at $Y/day (Finance, please advise if we need an approval; Kimberly I'll loop you for final pricing negotiation).

Rishi — can you open the quota exception ticket by EOD today with the following numbers:
- nova_critical route peak allowance: 5x baseline throughput, burst headroom to cover 220 concurrent spikes
- nova_best_effort route: 2x baseline (quantized model)
- Warm-up schedule attached in the ticket.

Customer confirmation (forwarded):
